slice: rmcp-v3.1.4 cooperative cancellation observable-state and persistent-cancel-fence contract

finding.observation: Exact rmcp-v3.1.4 cancellation tests and implementation make tasks/cancel acknowledgement non-terminal. TaskManager::cancel_task records cancel_requested and signals the operation, then returns immediately. A tasks/get immediately after the acknowledgement is explicitly tested to remain nonterminal; cancellation does not force the Task status to cancelled. The operation later determines the terminal outcome: TaskExit::Cancelled -> cancelled, TaskExit::Error -> failed, and successful completion despite the request -> completed.
finding.scope: Stock rmcp TaskManager cooperative-cancellation semantics at release commit 4a738b9d; not a claim about custom persistent handlers or external side-effect cancellation.
minimum_persistent_application_contract_: Authorize the task owner/principal before accepting cancellation.
Persist cancellation intent for the stable task identity before returning the cancellation acknowledgement; an in-memory flag alone is insufficient across server restart.
Every restart/redrive/claim path must consult the persisted cancellation record before starting or taking over further work for that task.
Use a monotonic attempt/generation fence (or equivalent CAS) so completion/status writes from a superseded attempt cannot overwrite the post-cancel state.

Do not treat the cancellation acknowledgement as proof that an already-entered external effect stopped. Non-idempotent external effects still require their own idempotency/fencing contract because a cooperative task may complete or fail after cancellation was requested.
finding.observable_state_boundary: Immediately after cancel_task returns, tasks/get may still report a nonterminal state. Later terminal state is allowed to be cancelled, failed, or completed depending on operation behavior.
